source_refs.note: Exercise 2.1, Question 16 (i)-(iv): derivatives with inverse trigonometric functions; 'Point to Note' box beside Q16; book p. 41. No printed answers.

blocks.explanation:
Yeh inverse trigonometric function ka sawal hai: \(\sin^{-1}\) ke andar \(\frac{x}{a}\) hai, jahan \(a\) ek constant hai.
Diya kya hai? \(\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)\). Find kya karna hai? Is ka derivative \(x\) ke respect se.
Rule kaunsa? Section 2.4 ka formula (i) \(\frac{d}{du}(\sin^{-1}u) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^2}}\), aur chain rule kyunke andar \(u = \frac{x}{a}\) hai.
Plan: \(u\) rakhenge, formula lagayenge, phir root ko saaf karenge. Hum \(a > 0\) maan kar chalenge, jo aam taur par hota hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)\), \(a > 0\), \(-a < x < a\).
Maloom karna: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: chain rule. \(-a < x < a\) isliye ke \(\sin^{-1}\) ke andar wali cheez \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan honi chahiye.

Substitution
\[u = \dfrac{x}{a},\quad \dfrac{du}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{a}\]
Kyun: \(a\) constant hai, to \(\frac{x}{a}\) ka derivative sirf \(\frac{1}{a}\).

Chain rule
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \frac{x^2}{a^2}}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{a}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{dy}{du} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^2}}\) mein \(u^2 = \frac{x^2}{a^2}\) rakha, aur \(\frac{du}{dx} = \frac{1}{a}\) se multiply kiya.
Dhyan dein: andar ka derivative \(\frac{1}{a}\) bhool jana sab se aam ghalti hai.

Root ko saaf karein
\[\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{x^2}{a^2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}}{a}\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{a} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}}\]
Kyun: \(1 - \frac{x^2}{a^2} = \frac{a^2 - x^2}{a^2}\), aur \(\sqrt{a^2} = a\) kyunke \(a > 0\). Fraction ulta ho kar upar \(a\) aaya jo \(\frac{1}{a}\) se cancel ho gaya. Agar \(a < 0\) hota to \(\sqrt{a^2} = -a\), aur jawab \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}}\) ho jata.

Tasdeeq \(x = 0\) par
\[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a^2}} = \dfrac{1}{a}\]
Kyun: chhote angle par \(\sin^{-1}u \approx u\), to \(y \approx \frac{x}{a}\), jis ka slope \(\frac{1}{a}\) hai. Formula bhi yahi deta hai.

blocks.explanation:
Is part mein \(\csc^{-1}\) ke andar ek fraction hai. Yeh is exercise ka sab se mushkil part hai, is liye aahista chalenge.
Diya kya hai? \(\csc^{-1}\left(\frac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 1}\right)\). Find kya karna hai? Derivative \(x\) ke respect se.
Rule kaunsa? Section 2.4 ka formula (vi) \(\frac{d}{du}(\csc^{-1}u) = -\frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^2 - 1}}\) aur chain rule, jahan \(u = \frac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 1}\).
Plan: pehle \(\frac{du}{dx}\), phir \(|u|\sqrt{u^2 - 1}\) ko alag se saaf, phir multiply. Modulus (absolute value) ke nishan ko poore raste sambhal kar rakhna hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \csc^{-1}\left(\frac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 1}\right)\), \(x \neq 0, \pm 1\).
Maloom karna: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^2 - 1}}\cdot\frac{du}{dx}\). \(x = \pm 1\) par fraction toot jata hai, aur \(x = 0\) par derivative nahi banta (wahan graph mein kona hai).

\(\frac{du}{dx}\) quotient rule se
\[\dfrac{du}{dx} = \dfrac{2x(x^2 - 1) - (x^2 + 1)2x}{(x^2 - 1)^2}\]
\[= \dfrac{-4x}{(x^2 - 1)^2}\]
Kyun: upar \(2x^3 - 2x - 2x^3 - 2x\); \(x^3\) wali terms cancel aur \(-4x\) bacha.

Root wala hissa
\[u^2 - 1 = \dfrac{(x^2 + 1)^2 - (x^2 - 1)^2}{(x^2 - 1)^2}\]
\[= \dfrac{4x^2}{(x^2 - 1)^2}\]
\[\sqrt{u^2 - 1} = \dfrac{2|x|}{|x^2 - 1|}\]
Kyun: \(u^2 - 1\) ko ek fraction banaya. Upar identity \((A + B)^2 - (A - B)^2 = 4AB\) lagi, \(A = x^2\), \(B = 1\), to \(4x^2\). Square root lete waqt \(\sqrt{p^2} = |p|\), is liye modulus aaya.
Dhyan dein: \(\sqrt{x^2}\) ko seedha \(x\) likhna ghalat hai; \(x\) negative ho sakta hai, is liye \(|x|\) likhna zaroori hai (kitab ka Recall box yahi kehta hai).

\(u\) ka modulus
\[|u| = \dfrac{x^2 + 1}{|x^2 - 1|}\]
\[|u|\sqrt{u^2 - 1} = \dfrac{2|x|(x^2 + 1)}{(x^2 - 1)^2}\]
Kyun: \(x^2 + 1\) hamesha positive hai, to modulus sirf neeche wale par laga. Phir dono ko multiply kiya; \(|x^2 - 1| \cdot |x^2 - 1| = (x^2 - 1)^2\).

Chain rule
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{(x^2 - 1)^2}{2|x|(x^2 + 1)} \cdot \dfrac{-4x}{(x^2 - 1)^2}\]
\[= \dfrac{2x}{|x|(1 + x^2)}\]
Kyun: formula ka minus aur \(\frac{du}{dx}\) ka minus mil kar plus bane. \((x^2 - 1)^2\) cancel, aur \(\frac{4}{2} = 2\).

Modulus ke baghair likhein
\[x > 0:\ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2}{1 + x^2}\]
\[x < 0:\ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{2}{1 + x^2}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{x}{|x|}\) positive \(x\) ke liye 1 aur negative ke liye \(-1\) hai. Yani jawab ki shakal \(x\) ke sign par depend karti hai.

Tasdeeq doosre raste se
\[y = \sin^{-1}w,\quad w = \dfrac{x^2 - 1}{x^2 + 1}\]
\[\dfrac{dw}{dx} = \dfrac{4x}{(x^2 + 1)^2},\ \sqrt{1 - w^2} = \dfrac{2|x|}{x^2 + 1}\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^2 + 1}{2|x|} \cdot \dfrac{4x}{(x^2 + 1)^2} = \dfrac{2x}{|x|(x^2 + 1)}\]
Kyun: \(\csc^{-1}u = \sin^{-1}\frac{1}{u}\), yani fraction ulta kar ke \(\sin^{-1}\) bana sakte hain. Is raste se bhi wohi jawab aaya, aur sympy ne \(x = \pm\frac{1}{2}, 2, -3\) par numbers se bhi tasdeeq ki.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Question 16 ke saath 'Point to Note' box mein likha hai ke \(x \in (-\infty, -1) \cup (1, \infty)\) ke liye \(\left|\frac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 1}\right| = \frac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 1} > 1\) (yeh sahi hai), aur yeh ke \(\frac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 1} < -1\) ka koi hal nahi. Doosri baat ghalat hai: jab \(0 < |x| < 1\) ho to neeche wala hissa negative hota hai. Misaal: \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) par \(\frac{5/4}{-3/4} = -\frac{5}{3}\), jo \(-1\) se chhota hai. Asal mein \(|x| < 1\) par hamesha \(\frac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 1} \leq -1\) hota hai (sirf \(x = 0\) par barabar \(-1\)). Is liye function har \(x \neq \pm 1\) par define hai, aur derivative \(\frac{2x}{|x|(1 + x^2)}\) har \(x \neq 0, \pm 1\) par sahi hai, sirf \(|x| > 1\) par nahi.

blocks.prompt: 16 (iii) Differentiate w.r.t. the variables involved: \(\cot^{-1}\left(\sqrt{x}\right) + \sqrt{\cot^{-1} x}\)
blocks.explanation:
Do terms hain aur dono composite, lekin layers ulti tarteeb mein: bilkul Question 10 jaisa.
\(\cot^{-1}(\sqrt{x})\) mein bahar \(\cot^{-1}\), andar \(\sqrt{x}\). \(\sqrt{\cot^{-1}x}\) mein bahar root, andar \(\cot^{-1}x\).
Rule kaunsa? Formula (iv) \(\frac{d}{du}(\cot^{-1}u) = -\frac{1}{1 + u^2}\) aur har term par chain rule.
Plan: har term alag, phir jama.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \cot^{-1}(\sqrt{x}) + \sqrt{\cot^{-1}x}\), \(x > 0\).
Maloom karna: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: sum rule aur chain rule. \(x > 0\) isliye ke \(\sqrt{x}\) chahiye aur us ka derivative \(x = 0\) par nahi banta.

Pehli term
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\cot^{-1}(\sqrt{x}) = -\dfrac{1}{1 + x} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}(1 + x)}\]
Kyun: \(u = \sqrt{x}\) ho to \(u^2 = x\), is liye \(1 + u^2 = 1 + x\). Andar ka derivative \((\sqrt{x})' = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\).

Doosri term
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\cot^{-1}x)^{1/2}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{\cot^{-1}x}} \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}\right)\]
Kyun: bahar \(w^{1/2}\), \(w = \cot^{-1}x\); root ka derivative \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{w}}\), darja \((\cot^{-1}x)' = -\frac{1}{1 + x^2}\). \(\cot^{-1}x\) ki range \((0, \pi)\) hai, yani hamesha positive, to root theek hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\sqrt{\cot^{-1}x}\) aur \(\cot^{-1}\sqrt{x}\) mein farq hai; pehle dekhiye root kis cheez par laga hai.

Jama karein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}(1 + x)}\]
\[\quad - \dfrac{1}{2(1 + x^2)\sqrt{\cot^{-1}x}}\]
Kyun: sum rule.

Sign ki tasdeeq
\[\text{both terms} < 0\]
Kyun: \(\cot^{-1}\) ghatne wala (decreasing) function hai, to \(x\) barhne par dono terms chhoti hoti hain. Is liye derivative ka negative hona bilkul theek hai.

blocks.prompt: 16 (iv) Differentiate w.r.t. the variables involved: \((\tan t)^{-1} + \frac{1}{\tan^{-1} t}\)
blocks.explanation:
Variable \(t\) hai, to \(\frac{dy}{dt}\) chahiye. Is part ka asal imtihaan notation parhna hai.
\((\tan t)^{-1}\) ka matlab \(\frac{1}{\tan t} = \cot t\) hai (reciprocal), jabke \(\tan^{-1}t\) inverse tangent hai (woh angle jis ka tan \(t\) ho).
Is liye \(y = \cot t + (\tan^{-1}t)^{-1}\).
Plan: \((\cot t)' = -\csc^2 t\), aur doosri term par power rule ke saath chain rule, \((\tan^{-1}t)' = \frac{1}{1 + t^2}\).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = (\tan t)^{-1} + \frac{1}{\tan^{-1}t}\), \(t \neq 0\).
Maloom karna: \(\frac{dy}{dt}\).
Tareeqa: pehle dono terms ko pehchaan kar nayi shakal mein likhenge, phir term by term derivative.

Nayi shakal
\[(\tan t)^{-1} = \cot t\]
\[\dfrac{1}{\tan^{-1}t} = (\tan^{-1}t)^{-1}\]
Kyun: bracket par \(-1\) power ka matlab 'ek bata', jabke \(\tan\) ke saath chipka \(^{-1}\) inverse function ka nishan hai. Bracket ki jagah sab kuch batati hai.

Pehli term
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}(\cot t) = -\csc^2 t\]
Kyun: Question 1(c) mein yahi derive kiya tha.

Doosri term
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}(\tan^{-1}t)^{-1} = -(\tan^{-1}t)^{-2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{1 + t^2}\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{(1 + t^2)(\tan^{-1}t)^2}\]
Kyun: bahar \(w^{-1}\) hai, \(w = \tan^{-1}t\); power rule se \(-w^{-2}\), darja andar ka derivative \(\frac{1}{1 + t^2}\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{1}{\tan^{-1}t}\) ko \(\tan t\) samajh lena bari ghalti hai; inverse function ka ulta (reciprocal) asal function nahi hota.

Jama karein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -\csc^2 t - \dfrac{1}{(1 + t^2)(\tan^{-1}t)^2}\]
Kyun: sum rule. Sympy ki tasdeeq bhi yahi jawab deti hai.
